t: One lion, 100 men, and one guy with a strength of 1,000.
Dropped into the middle of the Amazon rainforest, 30 days.
No food, no phones, no weapons.
Every player gets a wristband with one red button.
Press it, and a helicopter takes you home.
But you're out.
The question the whole internet keeps arguing about.
Who actually survives the jungle?
On Day 29, all three of them will end up at the same river
in the same flood at the same moment.
And what happens there will surprise everyone.
But first, let's meet the players.
Player 1, the lion.
200 kilos of muscle, teeth, and attitude.
He can run 60 kilometers an hour in short bursts.
His roar can be heard 8 kilometers away.
On the savannah, he's the king.
Player 2, 100 ordinary men.
A plumber, a dentist, a pizza delivery guy.
Two accountants, a math teacher, and 94 other guys
who have never slept outside in their lives.
The loudest one is Danny, a car salesman from Ohio.
The quietest one is Sam, who grew up on a farm
and hasn't said a word yet.
Player 3, Max.
16 years old.
A hundred times stronger than a normal human.
Some of you know him from last time.
He once lifted a steel door with a lever his brother designed.
But this time, his brother isn't here.
No Theo, no plan, just muscles.
Day 1, the helicopter disappears and the jungle closes in.
The lion has the first problem, and he doesn't even know it yet.
Lions don't live in rainforests.
They're built for open grassland, where they can see prey from far away.
Here, he can't see more than 10 meters in any direction.
Trees, vines, leaves, more leaves.
The king of the savannah looks around like a tourist who took the wrong bus.
The hundred men have a different problem.
They spend the first 40 minutes arguing about who's in charge.
Danny votes for Danny.
Danny wins.
Sam says nothing.
And Max?
Max punches a tree.
The tree falls.
He punches another one.
Within an hour, he's built a shelter out of whole logs,
with a roof so thick that nothing gets through.
He lies down inside and thinks, this is going to be easy.
Round 1, Shelter, Max.
Day 2, the heat.
The Amazon isn't just hot.
It's wet hot.
The air is so full of water that sweat can't dry off your skin.
And sweat only cools you down when it dries.
So your body keeps heating up, like a car engine with no radiator.
Max is thirsty.
There's water everywhere.
A river right next to his shelter.
He drinks, a lot.
The hundred men are thirsty too.
Danny walks toward the river.
And Sam finally speaks.
Don't.
Boil it first.
River water in the jungle is full of bacteria and parasites.
You can't see them.
You can't punch them.
The men spend six hours making fire by rubbing sticks together.
They take turns, 10 men at a time, until their hands are blistered.
When the first spark catches,
a hundred grown men cheer like they've won the World Cup.
They boil it in a pot the plumber made from river clay.
It's ugly.
It works.
On day three, Max can't get out of his shelter.
Fever, stomach cramps.
The strongest human on earth is lying on the floor,
defeated by something smaller than a grain of sand.
Strength doesn't fight germs.
Your immune system does.
And his is completely normal.
He doesn't press the button.
But he thinks about it.
Round two, water, the hundred men.
Day five, hunger.
The lion needs about seven kilos of meat a day.
On the savannah, he hunts zebras and antelopes.
Even there, most of his hunts fail.
Here, the prey is small, fast, and hidden.
On day five, he finally catches a capybara,
the world's biggest rodent.
It's not a zebra, but it's dinner.
The hundred men have the biggest problem of all.
A normal man needs about 2,500 calories a day.
Times a hundred, that's 250,000 calories every single day.
That's about 500 cheeseburgers.
In a jungle with no cheeseburgers.
They fish.
They catch almost nothing.
They try hunting a monkey with sticks.
The monkey throws fruit back at them.
Then, Sam shows them grubs.
Fat white larvae that live inside rotting palm trees.
They're full of protein and fat.
They taste like coconut, if coconut could wiggle.
Half the men eat them.
The other half go hungry.
And Max, finally feeling better,
finds a tree covered in round brown pods,
as hard as cannonballs.
Brazil nuts.
The pods are so tough that almost no animal can crack them.
Mostly just one small rodent with super sharp teeth.
Max squeezes one in his hand.
Crack!
Inside, 20 nuts.
He eats a hundred pods in a day.
Round three, food, Max.
Day eight, night.
Jungle nights are the loudest thing you've ever heard.
Frogs, insects, birds, howler monkeys screaming like someone is being robbed.
And somewhere in the dark, something is watching the men's camp.
A jaguar.
The biggest cat in the Americas.
Pound for pound, it has one of the strongest bites of any cat on earth.
Strong enough to crack a turtle shell.
Lions kill by choking their prey.
Jaguars often go straight for the skull.
The men don't see it.
They only see its eyes in the firelight.
Two yellow dots.
Then four.
Then gone.
By morning, 12 men have pressed their buttons.
Helicopters come and go all day.
88 left.
But the jaguar isn't the deadliest thing in the jungle.
The deadliest animal on earth weighs about two milligrams.
The mosquito.
Diseases spread by mosquitoes kill more people every year than any other animal
on the planet.
And then there's the bullet ant.
Its sting is often called the most painful insect sting in the world.
People say it feels like being shot.
On day 10, a math teacher sits on a nest.
He presses his button before he finishes screaming.
Max gets stung, too.
40 times.
He punches the air.
It doesn't help.
You can't win a fight against something you can't hit.
71 men left.
Day 12.
The lion meets the jaguar.
Two big cats, one riverbank.
The jaguar weighs about 100 kilos.
The lion weighs almost twice that.
In a fair fight out in the open, the lion probably wins.
But this isn't the open.
The jaguar climbs a tree and stares down at him.
Lions are bad climbers.
Jaguars are excellent ones.
They also swim.
And they even hunt caimans, which are small crocodiles.
The lion roars.
The jaguar yawns.
Then it disappears into the leaves like it was never there.
For the first time in his life, the king isn't the scariest thing around.
Day 14.
The fight the internet has been waiting for.
The lion is hungry.
Really hungry.
He's lost 20 kilos and he can smell 71 men all in one place.
He comes at night without a sound.
Danny sees him first.
And for the first time, the loudest man in the jungle can't make a sound.
But Sam stands up.
Fire! Everyone! Now!
Stand together!
71 men grab burning branches.
They don't run.
They make a wall.
Shoulder to shoulder, shouting as loud as they can, waving fire.
Most big cats won't attack a big group that stands its ground.
They're looking for something weak and alone.
And a wall of 71 screaming men holding fire
is not weak and not alone.
The lion stops.
Looks at the fire.
Looks at the men.
And slowly walks back into the dark.
One lion versus one man?
Lion. Every time.
One lion versus 100 men who work together?
That's a very different fight.
Round 4.
The lion versus the 100 men.
The men.
Day 18.
Max meets the lion.
On the same riverbank at the same time.
The lion is starving.
Max is alone.
They stare at each other.
The lion crouches.
Max could end this in one second.
One punch.
He doesn't.
He reaches into his pocket for a Brazil nut.
Then he remembers.
Lions don't eat nuts.
So Max catches a fish with his bare hands.
A big one!
And throws it across the river.
The lion sniffs it.
Eats it.
Looks at Max for a long time.
And leaves.
Round 5.
The jungle.
Nobody wins.
Day 20.
The jungle starts winning.
Everyone gets weaker in different ways.
The lion is now 30 kilos lighter.
His paws are cut.
And he hasn't slept properly in weeks.
On the savannah, lions sleep up to 20 hours a day.
Here, every sound wakes him.
The men start breaking.
Danny wants to march out of the jungle and find a road.
Sam says it's a terrible idea.
You can't see the sun under the trees,
and it's easy to walk in circles.
Danny calls Sam a farm boy.
30 men follow Danny.
Three days later, they press their buttons.
One by one.
Lost.
41 men left.
And Max?
Max has a different problem.
He's completely alone.
He starts talking to a rock.
He names it Theo.
Scientists have found that long periods of loneliness
can be as hard on the body as not sleeping or eating.
Max can lift a car.
He can't lift that.
Round 5.
The jungle.
Nobody wins.
Day 29.
It starts raining at midnight.
And it doesn't stop.
The Amazon gets more rain than almost anywhere on earth.
In the wet season,
rivers can rise several meters,
and huge parts of the forest go underwater.
By morning, the river is a monster.
The men's camp is gone.
41 men are standing on a muddy island
that's getting smaller every minute.
Sam knows there's high ground on the other side,
but the river is 50 meters wide and moving like a highway.
On a fallen tree in the middle of the river,
there's the lion.
Soaking wet, exhausted,
holding on with his claws.
Lions can swim, but not in this.
And on the far bank, safe on high ground, is Max.
He could just stay there, wait one more day,
win the whole game.
He looks at his wristband, then at the men,
then at the lion.
He walks into the river.
The water hits him like a truck.
He grabs the biggest tree on the bank,
the kind that takes 100 years to grow,
and pushes it over, right across the river.
The trunk crashes down onto the island.
A bridge!
Go! Sam shouts.
And 41 men run across a tree trunk in a flood,
holding each other's shirts one by one,
while Max holds the tree steady with both arms.
The last man crosses, and then Max looks back at the lion.
The fallen tree the lion is holding
is starting to break apart.
Max wades in, chest deep, then neck deep.
He grabs the lion by the scruff of the neck,
the way a mother lion carries her cubs.
200 kilos of wet, furious cat, and he swims.
On the bank, 41 men watch a teenager drag a lion out of a flood.
The lion coughs, shakes, looks at Max,
then walks to the men's fire and lies down next to it.
Nobody moves, nobody breathes, and the lion falls asleep.
Day 30.
The helicopters come.
So who survived the jungle?
The lion survived.
30 kilos lighter, but alive.
The jungle wasn't his home, and he still made it.
41 of the 100 men survived.
Not because they were strong, because they had fire,
a quiet farm boy who knew things, and each other.
And Max survived.
But here's what he learned.
Strength helped him build a house and crack nuts.
It didn't help with the germs, or the insects,
or the loneliness.
The two times he really mattered, it wasn't because he was strong.
It was because he chose to help.
So who actually wins?
Not the strongest, not the biggest.
The jungle doesn't care how strong you are.
It only cares whether you can work with others.
The last helicopter lands.
The pilot takes off his helmet.
It's Theo.
You named a rock after me?
It was a good rock.
Get in, mom's furious.
And our sister did something.
You need to see it.
So who would you bet on?
The lion, the 100 men, or Max?
Tell us in the comments.
And if you'd have jumped into that river too,
hit like and subscribe for the next one.
